questions.q: What is true of authentication on a freshly installed MongoDB instance, per this lesson?
options: It is enabled by default with a random generated password
It is disabled by default — anyone who can reach the port has full read/write access with no credentials
MongoDB cannot run at all without authentication configured first
Authentication is only ever optional for the admin database
questions.explain: A fresh MongoDB install has authentication off by default, a real and well-documented cause of exposed databases.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend creating the first administrative user before enabling authentication?
options: createUser() only works when authorization is already enabled
Because auth starts disabled, you can create that first user while it's still off, then turn authorization on
It's not actually necessary — order doesn't matter
MongoDB requires auth to already be enabled before any user can be created
questions.explain: The workflow is: create the admin user while auth is still off, then flip security.authorization to enabled.

questions.q: What does the --authenticationDatabase flag specify when connecting with mongosh?
options: Which database the query results will be returned from
The name of the database to delete on login
The TLS certificate authority to trust
Which database to check the user's credentials against, since users are created scoped to a specific database
questions.explain: MongoDB users are created in a specific database, and --authenticationDatabase tells mongosh which one to check credentials against.

questions.q: What is SCRAM in the context of MongoDB authentication?
options: A deprecated authentication method removed in modern MongoDB versions
A MongoDB Atlas-exclusive networking protocol
MongoDB's default authentication mechanism (SCRAM-SHA-256 by default since v4.0), which never sends the password itself over the wire
A backup format for encrypted MongoDB data
questions.explain: SCRAM (Salted Challenge Response Authentication Mechanism) is MongoDB's default auth protocol, using salted hashed challenge-response instead of transmitting the password.

questions.q: What does passwordPrompt() do when used inside db.createUser()?
options: Forces the user to change their password on next login
Interactively prompts for the password instead of putting it in plain text in shell history
Disables password authentication for that user
Automatically generates and emails a password to the new user
questions.explain: passwordPrompt() avoids exposing the plaintext password in the shell command or its history.
